get.description:
This finder can be used to retrieve a page of learning assets, given some set of criteria. Using this endpoint you can:

Search for learning assets given some search and relevance criteria.  
Retrieve a list of learning assets released, retired or modified since a given date.  
Retrieve a list of learning assets the requester is licensed to access.

GET [https://api.linkedin.com/v2/learningAssets?q=criteria](https://api.linkedin.com/v2/learningAssets?q=criteria)

Documentation: [https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/learning/reference/learningassets#criteria](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/learning/reference/learningassets#criteria)

*Access to LinkedIn Learning APIs is available to members of our [Partner Program](https://learning.linkedin.com/partners) and organizations that have purchased LinkedIn Learning site licenses.*

To retrieve a page of learning assets, given some criteria, issue a GET call to the following endpoint:
GET https://api.linkedin.com/v2/learningAssets?q=localeAndType

Documentation: https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/learning/integrations/locale-and-type-api#learningassets-localeandtype-finder

*Access to LinkedIn Learning APIs is available to members of our [Partner Program](https://learning.linkedin.com/partners) and organizations that have purchased LinkedIn Learning site licenses.*

parameters.name: assetFilteringCriteria.assetTypes[0]
parameters.description: An array of types of learning assets to search. The search results will include only learning assets of these types. The values of this parameter should be COURSE, LEARNING_PATH, or VIDEO.

parameters.name: assetFilteringCriteria.licensedOnly
parameters.description: Boolean that indicates results should be filtered to only include learningAssets the caller is licensed to access. If this parameter is set to true and assetFilteringCriteria.locales parameter is omitted the locale values are implied by the callers licensed access.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: The number of learning assets to include in the page. Please choose a reasonable value if overriding the default; the API will return an error if the requested page exceeds the 2 MB response size limit of the framework.

parameters.name: expandDepth
parameters.description: The number of levels in the learning asset hierarchy to include asset details. This parameter is optional; please see the Specifying the level of asset details section for an explanation with examples.

parameters.name: includeRetired
parameters.description: Whether to include retired learning assets. The value of this parameter should be true or false.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Value of this parameter should always be criteria

The value of this parameter should always be: localeAndType.

parameters.name: sourceLocale.country
parameters.description: The locale country of the learning assets. The value of this parameter should be DE, US, ES, FR, or JP. These values correspond to the locales "de_DE", "en_US", "es_ES", "fr_FR", and "ja_JP".

parameters.name: sourceLocale.language
parameters.description: The locale language of the learning assets. The value of this parameter should be de, en, es, fr, or ja. These values correspond to the locales "de_DE", "en_US", "es_ES", "fr_FR", and "ja_JP".

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: The start index of learning assets for the page.

This API Call is for creating Promoted Jobs by mentioning `listingType` as `PREMIUM`. `Contract URN` is mandatory field for this call. Customer can include `posterEmail` and `showPosterInfo` as field Parameter. Please refer [here](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/job-posting-api-schema#promoted-jobs-extension-schema)

This call is for Syncing PUBLIC Jobs to LinkedIn from ATS. `availability` field set to `PUBLIC`. Please refer [here](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/job-posting-api-schema#recruiter-system-connect-extension-schema)

In order to update a simple job posting, you can just re-post the job with any changed information and `jobPostingOperationType` field value set as `UPDATE` .Please refer [here](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/update-renew-jobs)

To renew a job, re-post it with `jobPostingOperationType` field as `RENEW` and no other changes. The renewal operation extends the expiration of job posts by 30 days. .Please refer [here](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/update-renew-jobs)

There are two alternate ways to renew job postings:

Close previous jobs, and re-post jobs without any changes
Publish new jobs with different `externalJobPostingId`

To close a job, re-post the job using same `externalJobPostingId` value, but set jobPostingOperationType to `CLOSE`.Please refer [here](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/close-jobs)

The maximum number of jobs which can be submitted during one batch call is 100. If you would like to submit more than 100 jobs at a time, please group your jobs in to collections of 100 and make multiple batch calls in sequential order. To know more, please refer [here](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/job-postings/api/create-jobs#sample-request-for-basic-jobs)

#### Request Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |

In the event of a successful request, the response will contain the following fields:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| owner | String | The owner of the lead generation form |
| hiddenFields | Array | An array of hidden fields, each containing a name and value |
| versionId | Integer | The version ID of the lead generation form |
| created | Integer | The timestamp of when the lead generation form was created |
| creationLocale | Object | An object containing the country and language of the lead generation form |
| name | String | The name of the lead generation form |
| id | Integer | The unique identifier of the lead generation form |
| lastModified | Integer | The timestamp of when the lead generation form was last modified |
| state | String | The current state of the lead generation form |
| content | Object | An object containing the content of the lead generation form, including questions, description, legal information, and headline |

The 'content' object contains the following fields:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| questions | Array | An array of questions, each containing a question ID, localized question text, response editability, name, question details, and predefined field |
| description | Object | An object containing the localized description of the lead generation form |
| legalInfo | Object | An object containing consents, legal information ID, privacy policy URL, and legal disclaimer |
| headline | Object | An object containing the localized headline of the lead generation form |

Each question object in the 'questions' array contains the following fields:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| questionId | Integer | The question ID |
| question | Object | An object containing the localized question text |
| responseEditable | Boolean | Indicates whether the response is editable |
| name | String | The name of the question |
| questionDetails | Object | An object containing details about the question, such as max response length |
| predefinedField | String | The predefined field of the question |
| responseRequired | Boolean | Indicates whether a response is required |

The 'legalInfo' object contains the following fields:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| consents | Array | An array of consents, each containing a consent object with localized consent text and check requirement |
| legalInfoId | Integer | The legal information ID |
| privacyPolicyUrl | String | The URL of the privacy policy |
| legalDisclaimer | Object | An object containing the localized legal disclaimer |

In the event of an error, the response will contain an empty object.

[Ad Analytics APIs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/marketing/integrations/ads-reporting/ads-reporting) provide key insights on performance such as clicks, impressions, and ad spend, and demographics information such as metrics by demographic values at the account, campaign, and creative levels.

The /adAnalytics endpoint supports two finder methods: Analytics and Statistics. The [Analytics Finder](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/marketing/integrations/ads-reporting/ads-reporting#analytics-finder) should be used when grouping by one element (known as a pivot). The [Statistics Finder](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/marketing/integrations/ads-reporting/ads-reporting#statistics-finder) should be used when grouping by up to three elements.

The /adAnalytics endpoint will require you to define [Field Projections](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/shared/api-guide/concepts/projections?context=linkedin/marketing/context) using the &fields= query parameter and narrowed by providing a comma-separated list of field names that you want to return. You can specify up to 20 fields in the response.

The response may contain URNs referencing the different types of objects provided by LinkedIn's services. You can use the [Response Decoration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/shared/api-guide/concepts/decoration?context=linkedin/marketing/context) to fetch data belonging to a URN object without having to make an extra call to that object's API.

tags.name: Use Cases / Advertising and Targeting / Ads Targeting
tags.description:
LinkedIn's [Ad Targeting API](https://docs.microsoft.com/linkedin/marketing/integrations/ads/advertising-targeting/ads-targeting?tabs=http&view=li-lms-unversioned) enables advertisers to better control which audiences see their ads. These controls include a variety of member demographics in the LinkedIn platform. Targeting is set at the campaign level, and applies to all creatives associated with that campaign.

**The two core concepts for targeting are facets and entities.**

\*   Facets are high-level categories of the types of targeting available to you.
\*   Facets contain multiple entities which are the specific demographic values within that facet.
    

For example, Industries is a facet. Specific industries such as Computer Software, Biotechnology, and Telecommunications are entities within the Industries facet.

tags.name: Use Cases / Advertising and Targeting / Ads Forecasting
tags.description:
The [Ad Supply Forecasts API](https://docs.microsoft.com/linkedin/marketing/integrations/ads/advertising-targeting/ad-supply-forecasts?tabs=http&view=li-lms-unversioned) enables you to forecast impressions, spending, and other metrics based on:

\*   Targeting criteria
\*   Campaign settings such as campaign type and objective type
\*   Bid and spending settings
\*   Time period
    

To calculate the forecast, we analyze these data points for your campaign, take into account campaign performance from similar campaigns/advertisers, and simulate the ad auction and serving processes. While we aim for utmost accuracy in our forecasts, it’s important to remember that forecasted results are an estimate and do not guarantee the actual performance of your campaign.

tags.name: Use Cases / Organic
tags.description:
In order to support collecting leads for organic use cases (company/showcase page, events, or product pages), a partner app needs to build a UX where a user is able to select the organizations and forms to collect leads for.

###### Step 1: Obtain user authorization to access their leads

###### Step 2: Ask the user what lead types they would like to sync - Events (EVENT), company/showcase pages (COMPANY), Product pages (ORGANIZATION_PRODUCT)

###### Step 3: Get the user's Organization(s) and validate their role to sync leads

###### Step 4: Ask the user to select the organization(s) whose leads they are interested in syncing

###### Step 5: Retrieve forms for the user's selected organization

###### Step 6: Ask the user to select and map fields to the target destination (e.g. a CRM)

###### Step 7: Allow the user to do a one time pull of all form responses looking back up to 365 days to grab any missed leads for the chosen lead types

###### Step 8: \[PULL\] Schedule periodic form response pulls to collect leads

###### Step 8: \[PUSH\] Allow the user to subscribe for lead notification webhooks

###### Step 9: \[PUSH\] Fetch full lead data after a webhook notification is received

tags.name: Ad Targeting Entities
tags.description:
The LinkedIn ads platform allows advertisers to target different types of audiences on the professional network. The two core concepts for targeting are facets and entities.

Facets are high-level categories of the types of targeting available to you. Facets contain multiple entities which are the specific demographic values within that facet. For example, Industries is a facet. Specific industries such as Computer Software, Biotechnology, and Telecommunications are entities within the Industries facet.

Use facets to narrow down your intended audience. Refer to [Targeting Criteria Facet URNs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/shared/references/v2/ads/targeting-criteria-facet-urns?view=li-lms-2023-09) for the list of available facets and their URNs. The `adTargetingFacets` API returns available targeting facets.

Once you've identified the facet type(s) you'd like to target, you can fetch their entity values. Use the `adTargetingEntities` API to fetch available options for each facet type. To learn more, see [Ad Targeting Entities](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/shared/references/v2/ads/adtargetingentities?context=linkedin%2Fmarketing%2Fcontex&view=li-lms-2023-09).

### Permissions

Any application approved for the LinkedIn Marketing API Program can make these API calls using any 3-legged access token. No additional permissions need to be requested during the OAuth flow.

tags.name: Fetch Audience Insights
tags.description:
Audience Insights API provides aggregated demographic insights, firmographic details, location and interests / behaviors of a target audience. The insights are primarily comprised of the below categories :

- Member Insights (Job Function, Title, Seniority, Years Of Experience, Skills)
    
- Company Insights (Company Name, Industry, Size, Growth rate)
    
- Location Insights (City, State, Country/Region, Continent)
    
- Member Interests (General and Product Interest categories derived from engagement behaviors and profile information)

tags.name: Conversion Events Streaming Workflow
tags.description:
1. Obtain user authorization with consent to create and manage conversions using `rw_conversions`, `r_ads` permissions in the scope.
    
2. Retrieve authenticated user's sponsored Ad Accounts where user has a non-viewer user role in the ad account.
    
3. Ask the user to select one of their Ad Account where conversion events would be streamed.
    
4. Fetch existing active Conversion Rules for CAPI in the selected Ad Account
    
5. Allow the user to choose if they want to create a new Conversion Rule or update an existing one
    

- If user chose to create a new conversion rule, otherwise jump to step 8:
    

6a. Create a new Conversion Rule with auto association to all campaigns  
(if successful, jump to step 8)

or

6b. Create a new Conversion Rule with auto association to campaigns based on conversion type (mapped to campaign objectives)

(if successful, jump to step 8)

or

6c. Create a new Conversion Rule with no campaign association (only required if auto association with all campaigns was not used)

(if successful, continue to step 7)

- Skip step 7 if the user chose to auto assoicate campaigns or update an existing Conversion Rule
    

7a. Fetch active campaign URNs to associate with conversion rule

7b. Ask the user to select specific campaigns (by default select all campaigns)

7c. Associate campaigns to conversion rule for campaign attribution and optimization

7d. For multiple campaigns, Batch Associate multiple campaigns to conversion rule for campaign attribution and optimization

- Send conversion events data (recurring)
    

8a. Stream conversion event to the conversion rule

8b. Stream multiple conversion events to the conversion rule

tags.description:
Candidates should be synced to the Middleware Platform whenever they are created or updated in your Talent CRM connect.

For more details, please see the [Sync Candidate documentation.](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/crm-connect/sync-crm-candidates?context=linkedin/talent/crm-connect/full_context/context)

tags.name: Sync TCRM Pipelines
tags.description:
Pipelines (or the equivalent in your system) should be synced to the Middleware Platform whenever they are created or updated in your Talent CRM Connect. We define a pipeline as any feature that is used for nurturing and sourcing candidates. Other terms for pipeline include talent pool and folder.

For more details, please see the [Sync Pipelines document.](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/crm-connect/sync-crm-pipelines?context=linkedin/talent/crm-connect/full_context/context)

tags.name: Sync TCRM PipelineStages
tags.description:
Pipeline Stages should be sent via the Middleware Platform whenever a new stage is created or an existing stage is updated in your Talent CRM.

For more details, please see the [Sync PipelineStages document](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/crm-connect/sync-crm-pipeline-stages?context=linkedin/talent/crm-connect/full_context/context).

tags.name: Sync TCRM CandidatePipelines
tags.description:
The Candidate Pipeline endpoint represents information about a candidate that is specific to a single pipeline. A candidate’s pipeline information should be synced to the Middleware Platform whenever a candidate is added to, removed from, or updated inside a pipeline in your Talent CRM.

For more details, please see the [Sync CandidatePipelines document.](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/crm-connect/sync-crm-candidate-pipelines?context=linkedin/talent/crm-connect/full_context/context)

tags.name: Sync TCRM CandidatePipelineStages
tags.description:
The Candidate Pipeline Stages endpoint represents information about a candidate that is specific to a single pipeline and stage change. A candidate’s pipeline information should be synced to the Middleware Platform whenever a candidate stage changes inside a pipeline in your Talent CRM.

For more details, please see the [Sync CandidatePipelineStages document.](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/crm-connect/sync-crm-candidate-pipeline-stages?context=linkedin%2Ftalent%2Fcrm-connect%2Ffull_context%2Fcontext)

tags.name: Sync TCRM CandidateResumes
tags.description:
To upload a resume, you first need to get a signed URL from LinkedIn and then use it to upload the file. When uploading resume, LinkedIn recommends to abide by the following considerations:

- Supported media formats are: PDF, DOC, or TXT
- Ensure that the media file size does not exceed 10MB for all file types
- Upload only one resume object per API call
- Ensure that all calls to upload resume use OAuth 2.0 authentication
    

For more details, please see the [Sync CandidateResunes document.](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/crm-connect/sync-crm-candidate-resumes?context=linkedin/talent/crm-connect/full_context/context)

tags.name: Sync TCRM interactions
tags.description:
Interactions include any means by which a candidate has interacted with a recruiter, a candidate has interacted with a company, or a recruiter has updated a candidate’s profile within the Talent CRM system (e.g., recruiter tags and notes). All of the interactions that fall into these categories should be sent via the Middleware Platform whenever they are created or updated in your CRM system.

For more details, please see the [Sync Interactions document.](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/linkedin/talent/crm-connect/sync-crm-interactions?context=linkedin/talent/crm-connect/full_context/context)
